title: Noma Security Discloses Claude Code Desktop Exploit
key_facts: Noma Security found a flaw, called SneakPeek, in Anthropic's Claude Code Desktop app.
Malicious JavaScript in an HTML file could run in the app's preview pane without further user action and read local files.
HTML files over 256KB were loaded as file:// URLs, bypassing the content security policy applied to smaller files.
Data at risk included cloud credentials, GitHub secrets and SSH private keys.
The flaw has a CVSS score of 8.7 (high), assigned by Anthropic; a CVE ID is not yet available.
Noma says Anthropic worked with it and fully fixed the issue; an initial patch was bypassed and a deeper fix followed.
Anthropic did not immediately comment to CSO.
quote_evidence: Simply asking Anthropic's Claude Code to review an HTML file could hand attackers access to a developer's machine, cloud credentials and software development environment, according to a new Noma Security finding.
Noma says Anthropic collaborated with Noma Labs during the disclosure process and fully resolved the issue.
why_it_matters_hint: A widely used AI coding tool could leak developers' secrets until patched.
notes: Claims come from Noma; Anthropic's confirmation is relayed by Noma, and Anthropic had not commented.
